title: One-step perfect finite quotient models and uniform propagation
statement: Let X be locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let (A,I) be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let M be an arbitrary complex of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf. Identify the constant finite coefficient sheaves with the actual coefficient sheaves by isomorphisms commuting with consecutive quotient maps and the completed scalar projections. Write M_n for the actual derived reduction to A/I^(n+1) [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Fix an etale chart V and a nonempty interval [a,b]. If M_0 and M_n admit etale local constant finite-projective complex models with terms in [a,b], then M_(n+1) admits such models in the same interval. No completeness of M or compatible trivializations is assumed. Consequently a residue-trivializing cover provides one interval on each chart that works at every finite level, by induction.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 094I, perfect-residue ideal-filtration argument; connected etale perfect constancy.

proof.text: Apply the finite-module model step to the residue and previous-level models, obtaining one covering sieve with bounded finite-module complexes P in [a,b]. On empty charts the chosen P is zero. This step does not claim projectivity.

On each chart apply algebraic Tor-amplitude detection from the residue to the displayed model P. The chart is nonempty or P is zero by the preceding step. Thus Q(P) has Tor amplitude [a,b]. Since the coefficient ring is finite it is Noetherian; apply the already proved bounded-finite-Tor perfectness theorem to replace P by a finite-projective complex E with terms in exactly [a,b].

The universe-lift and scalar-restriction functors are exact, as is constant module realization. Their exact derived functor maps the algebraic isomorphism Q(E)~Q(P) to the termwise constant realizations. Apply actual derived coefficient change and exact restriction, using the proved comparison with the representative-based restriction formula. Compose with the supplied model of the quotient reduction to obtain its required E model. Reuse the same covering sieve.

Normalization still gives the two coefficient compatibility equations by sheafification extensionality. For the uniform corollary keep the original residue cover, widen an empty interval to [min a b,b], use exact further restriction for the zero-level model, then induct on n using the successor theorem with this same interval.

proof_origin.place: Tags 094G and 094I, followed by the existing algebraic bounded finite Tor perfectness theorem (Tag 0658); D2 Lean reduction of the successor step

from.place: Uniform perfect finite quotient models from a perfect residue model

lean.statement:
theorem residuePerfect_quotient_models_succ
    (X : Scheme.{t}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X]
    {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    [∀ n : ℕ, (koszulConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))).PreservesZeroMorphisms]
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, adicConstantRing X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1)) ⟶
      completedAdicFiniteCommRing X d n)
    (_hφ : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (φ n)) (_hcompat : FinitePerfectModelsCompatible X d φ)
    (M : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules X d)) (V : X.Etale)
    (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b)
    (_hresidue : FinitePerfectModelsOn X d φ M 0 V a b) (n : ℕ)
    (_hprevious : FinitePerfectModelsOn X d φ M n V a b) :
    FinitePerfectModelsOn X d φ M (n + 1) V a b
